after: Classical cell-averaging and order-statistic constant-false-alarm-rate (CFAR) laws assume independent exponential samples. In correlated, textured clutter, autoregressive (AR) whitening and innovation-power normalization recover these laws under the true AR compound-Gaussian model with common episode texture and no thermal noise. We derive a post-onset law quantifying persistent-target contamination of a cell's own history; a slow-time guard delays self-masking by its length. Under exchangeability and a dominating, clutter-independent hit model, a conformal threshold on a worst-case bound certifies clipped and binary integration against pulsed interference of any power. Simulations and measurements of sea clutter and 77~GHz ground scenes test calibration, target visibility, noise and interference. On McMaster IPIX sea clutter, conformal thresholds keep 12 of 13 statistics within \LConfMinFour--\LConfMaxFour{} times design down to $10^{-4}$; \NWhitenedLawsFail{} of \NWhitenedLaws{} model-based laws exceed twice design, up to \LAnalMaxFour-fold. At $10^{-2}$, an eight-pulse guard raises mean per-look detection of an injected persistent 10~dB target over looks 1--8 from \GuardMeanLookZero{} to \GuardMeanLookEight, except at clutter Doppler; \LongLooks{}-look trajectories show later collapse. The guard benefit recurs on NetRAD S-band clutter, unused in initial development; \NetNOverTwoFourWord{} statistics exceed twice design at $10^{-4}$ after threshold refitting. With sparse real 77~GHz interference, certified clipping gives \JCertPfaC{} times design at a \JCertCostAll~dB overall sensitivity cost; fast-time zeroing restores clean-reference rates. Radar- and camera-labelled pedestrians show little whitening advantage at weak inter-frame correlation. Guarded acquisition remains poor under idealized continuous migration; burst-matched certification controls false alarms but detects no target.
